about: A default that depends on another flag. Lives on the target. Two arguments are presence; three are equality. First match wins. Command line and environment on the target suppress it. An applied default_if is a default, not an explicit value.

vectors.doc: `default_if "--json" "true"` binds when `--json` is given. clap's ArgPredicate::IsPresent.
With the selector absent, the target stays unset.
Three arguments: bind when the selector has that explicit value.
An unrelated value on the selector does not bind the default.
Conditions are tried in order; the first that matches binds.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "--style <s>" {
  default_if "--json" "compact"
  default_if "--pretty" "pretty"
}
flag "--json"
flag "--pretty"

vectors.doc: A value typed for the target wins over default_if.
The target's environment is a value, so it suppresses default_if.
A selector filled from the environment is present, so default_if binds. Env is applied to every flag before any default_if, so declaration order does not matter.
An applied default_if is a default. requires_if only reads command-line and environment values.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "--format <f>" {
  default_if "--json" "json"
  requires_if "json" "--schema"
}
flag "--schema <s>"
flag "--json"

vectors.doc: A positive requirement asks whether the other flag ended up with a value. default_if is a value, the same as an unconditional default.
vectors.spec:
name "ex" bin "ex" flag "--out

" requires="--format" flag "--format " { default_if "--json" "json" } flag "--json"

vectors.doc: When no condition matches, an unconditional default still applies.
An Equals default_if on a bool reads the negate form as false, the same way requires_if does. `--no-json` is given, and its value is false.
A bound default_if value is checked against choices the same way a default is.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "--color <when>" {
  default_if "--pretty" "rainbow"
  choices "auto" "always" "never"
}
flag "--pretty"
